## The source

- **Approximate formulas for some functions of prime numbers** — J. Barkley Rosser, Lowell Schoenfeld. Illinois Journal of Mathematics 6(1) (1962), 64–94; Corollary 3 equation (3.9), p. 69  
  _The paper identifies the left side as Bertrand’s postulate and the right side as Finsler’s bound, extended to real x, with uncovered ranges checked from prime tables. This proof uses Mathlib’s Bertrand theorem and an elementary binomial upper bound with a finite floor-based computation._

## Conclusions

### `equation_3_9`

**Corollary 3, equation (3.9), p. 69.** For every real `x > 1`,
`0 < π(2x) - π(x) < 7x / (5 log x)`. The count includes the right endpoint.
This is the complete two-sided inequality; both inequalities are strict.

```lean
def equation_3_9 : Prop :=
  ∀ x : ℝ, 1 < x →
    0 < IEANTN.primeCounting (2 * x) - IEANTN.primeCounting x ∧
      IEANTN.primeCounting (2 * x) - IEANTN.primeCounting x < 7 * x / (5 * Real.log x)
```
